keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the 1750 BC peak. The infobox gives 43,000 km2 for 1750 BC (peak c. 1752): 'By the middle of the 18th century BC, most of Syria minus the south came under the authority of Yamhad'. The shape (Aleppo, Idlib, Hatay, Lattakia and a 40 km circle at Raqqa for Tuttul) is the researcher's reading at 33,900 km2, ratio 0.79 to the infobox, within a factor of two; Hama and the Euphrates east of Raqqa are not added. The land beyond the core was held through vassal kings (ledger).

notes: Cliopatria has no Yamhad. The Ebla dossier (another group) is the first kingdom only; Ebla's third kingdom (c. 2000-1600), a vassal of Yamhad until Mursili I destroyed it c. 1600 BC, has no dossier. The 1750 BC peak is a union of modern provinces fitted to 'most of Syria minus the south' (33,900 km2 against the infobox 43,000); the vassal kings (Ebla, Mamma, Ugarit, Alalakh, Carchemish) are carried as one combined vassal event because no page dates them separately. Mursili I's c. 1600 sack of Halab is in the wars list only: the dynasty stayed at Halab, so no ledger event moves land or capital. The infobox ends the state c. 1517; the annexation under Parshatatar is c. 1524, used here. The mitanni dossier has Mitanni reaching Aleppo under Barattarna c. 1500-1480, about two decades after Parshatatar. Qatna 'remained independent' and has no dossier. Page budget: four pages.
